intended_object: The power set of a finite set s: the finite set of all subsets of s, with each subset itself a finite set. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition starts from `Multiset.powerset` of the underlying multiset `s.1`. For a multiset this gives every sub-multiset, counted with multiplicity. Each sub-multiset is a submultiset of the duplicate-free `s.1`, so it has no duplicates either, and `pmap Finset.mk` turns it into a finset. The resulting multiset of finsets has no repeats because `s.nodup.powerset` holds and `Finset.mk` is injective on underlying values. So the result is exactly the finset of all finsets `t` with `t ⊆ s`, which is the power set. It is stated for an arbitrary type `α` with no extra hypotheses, so it is at full generality. This is Mathlib's own canonical definition. The closest analogue for arbitrary sets is `Set.powerset` (𝒫); `Multiset.powerset` is the multiset version that this definition is built on.
